bib.title: LXMERT: Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers

question: Can large-scale pretraining of a dedicated cross-modality Transformer on image-text pairs yield a reusable backbone for vision-and-language reasoning?
hypothesis: Pretraining with diverse intra- and cross-modality tasks on a cross-modality architecture beats using BERT with vision heads and beats task-specific training.
contributions: LXMERT: Transformer with object-relationship, language and cross-modality encoders
Five pretraining tasks (masked cross-modality LM, RoI-feature regression, detected-label classification, cross-modality matching, image QA)
SotA on VQA and GQA, 22% absolute gain on NLVR2
Ablations on BERT use, image-QA pretraining, vision tasks

method.summary: A two-stream-then-fused Transformer: 9-layer language encoder, 5-layer object-relationship encoder over 36 Faster R-CNN objects, 5 cross-modality layers (cross-attn, self-attn, FF). Pretrained from scratch on 9.18M image-sentence pairs with five equally weighted losses, then fine-tuned on VQA, GQA, NLVR2.
method.task: vision-and-language pretraining; VQA, GQA, NLVR2 fine-tuning

datasets.name: Pretraining mix: MS COCO captions, Visual Genome captions, VQA v2.0, GQA balanced, VG-QA
datasets.size: 9.18M image-sentence pairs, 180K images, ~100M words, 6.5M image objects (COCO-Cap 617K, VG-Cap 5.39M, VQA 658K, GQA 1.07M, VG-QA 1.44M per Table 1 columns)
datasets.split: train and dev only; 5K COCO val images held out as minival; COCO test excluded
datasets.preprocessing: minimal; questions used as sentences, answers as labels; ~1/3 of sentences are questions; 9500-answer joint table covers ~90% of questions

datasets.name: VQA v2.0
datasets.split: same as pretraining split; minival for validation; test-dev and test-standard

datasets.name: GQA
datasets.split: testdev as validation, train+val for fine-tuning, test-standard

datasets.name: NLVR2
datasets.preprocessing: two image-statement pairs encoded separately, outputs concatenated

models.name: LXMERT
models.architecture: Transformer: language encoder NL=9, object-relationship encoder NR=5, cross-modality encoder NX=5
models.init_from: random (from scratch); BERT-init variant tested in ablation

other.object_detector: Faster R-CNN (101-layer, Visual Genome, Anderson et al. 2018), frozen

training.objective: Sum of five losses with equal weights: masked LM (p=0.15), masked object RoI-feature regression (L2) and detected-label classification (CE) (mask p=0.15), cross-modality matching (mismatch p=0.5), image QA

other.NLVR2 classifier: GeLU + LayerNorm head on concatenated [x0;x1], BCE loss

inference.samples: single model, not stated whether single run

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: VQA/GQA answer accuracy (Binary/Number/Other/Open sub-splits); NLVR2 label accuracy

metrics.name: consistency
metrics.definition: proportion of unique NLVR2 sentences for which all related image pairs are correctly predicted

eval.protocol: Test servers for VQA/GQA/NLVR2; ablations on dev sets; no seeds or significance tests reported

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests reported.
Ablation gains measured on dev sets with single runs.
Compared against SotA at the May 2019 submission; later models (MCAN 72.8% VQA) are noted as stronger.
Pretraining relies on a frozen Faster R-CNN with 36 objects and noisy detected labels.
Parameter count, heads and warmup not stated.
Mismatched sentences in matching task may rarely still match.
